prospects.name: Phil Knight (and Penny Knight)
prospects.uo_connection: B.B.A. 1959; ran middle-distance track under coach Bill Bowerman; member of Phi Gamma Delta; sports reporter for the Oregon Daily Emerald
prospects.current_role: Co-founder and Chairman Emeritus, Nike, Inc.; Chairman, Laika animation studio
prospects.location: Hillsboro/Beaverton, Oregon area (also La Quinta, California)
prospects.giving_capacity: >$500M to UO Athletics in a single transformational commitment
prospects.wealth_sources: Nike, Inc. — co-founded 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports; built into the world's largest athletic footwear/apparel brand. Wealth primarily from his Nike equity stake.
prospects.recent_news: In August 2025, Phil and Penny Knight pledged $2 billion to OHSU's Knight Cancer Institute, topping the Chronicle of Philanthropy's 2025 list of biggest gifts; their total OHSU giving now exceeds $2.7B. In late 2025 he made a record $3M political donation in Oregon.
prospects.athletics_connection: The single most important benefactor in UO Athletics history — established the $100M Athletics Legacy Fund (2007), funded Matthew Knight Arena (named for his late son), the Marcus Mariota Sports Performance Center ($19.2M), Hatfield-Dowlin Complex, Jaqua Center, Papé Field complex, and founded Division Street (the UO NIL collective). Has given over $1B to UO overall.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Has given $4B+ to charity; $2.7B to OHSU; over $1B to UO; $500M to the Knight Campus; $400M pledge to rebuild Portland's Albina neighborhood (2023).
prospects.why_prospect: Knight is the foundational mega-donor of UO Athletics and remains deeply, emotionally engaged with Ducks football, basketball and track at age 88. No prospect on earth has greater demonstrated capacity or affinity for the Forever Ducks program. He continues to make nine- and ten-figure gifts.
prospects.engagement_angle: Leverage the legacy/continuity theme — succession of his athletics vision, naming opportunities tied to family (as with Matthew Knight Arena), and the future of Division Street/NIL infrastructure as college athletics enters the revenue-sharing era.
prospects.urgency_flag: Age 88 — estate and legacy planning window is paramount; the recent $2B OHSU gift signals he is actively deploying capital at scale right now.

prospects.name: Connie Ballmer (and Steve Ballmer)
prospects.uo_connection: Connie Ballmer earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from UO in 1984; served on the UO Board of Trustees from 2014 to 2021; native Oregonian
prospects.current_role: Co-founder, Ballmer Group Philanthropy. Steve Ballmer is former CEO of Microsoft and owner of the LA Clippers.
prospects.giving_capacity: >$100M for a directed UO priority; capacity is effectively unlimited at the institutional level
prospects.wealth_sources: Microsoft equity (Steve Ballmer retained most of his stock after stepping down as CEO in 2014); LA Clippers franchise ownership.
prospects.recent_news: In April 2026, Connie Ballmer donated $80M to NPR (largest gift ever by a living donor to NPR). The couple have donated at least $8B through 2025. Their $425M UO gift created the Ballmer Institute for Children's Behavioral Health (announced 2022).
prospects.athletics_connection: No direct UO Athletics gift to date — their UO focus has been the Ballmer Institute (children's behavioral health). However, Steve Ballmer's deep sports ownership background (Clippers) and Connie's UO loyalty create a credible athletics affinity, especially around student-athlete wellness/mental health.
prospects.philanthropy_history: $425M to UO (Ballmer Institute); $175M youth economic mobility (2023); $80M to NPR (2026); $8B+ total via Ballmer Group, focused on economic mobility for children and families.
prospects.why_prospect: Connie is a UO alumna and former trustee with one of the largest fortunes on the planet and a demonstrated nine-figure giving record to UO specifically. While their giving is mission-driven (children, mobility, mental health), a student-athlete behavioral-health or wellness initiative within Athletics is a natural bridge.
prospects.engagement_angle: Frame the ask around student-athlete mental health and behavioral wellness — a tie-in to the Ballmer Institute mission — rather than facilities. Lead with measurable, data-driven outcomes, which align with the Ballmers' philanthropic style.
prospects.urgency_flag: Actively deploying billions annually; the recent NPR and OHSU-area giving shows the Pacific Northwest remains a focus. Their giving is data/impact-gated rather than time-gated.

Billionaire Connie Ballmer just donated $80 million to support NPR - Fortune, https://fortune.com/2026/04/20/connie-ballmer-npr-donation-80-million-trump-funding-cuts/
The Ballmer Gift - The Ballmer Institute, University of Oregon, https://childrensbehavioralhealth.uoregon.edu/ballmer-gift

prospects.name: Lorry I. Lokey (legacy/estate consideration)
prospects.uo_connection: One of the largest individual donors in UO history; the UO science complex is named the Lorry I. Lokey Science Complex; supported faculty excellence, the education quad, music building and more
prospects.current_role: Founder of Business Wire (deceased 2022); estate/foundation giving
prospects.location: California / Oregon (Business Wire was San Francisco-based)
prospects.estimated_net_worth: Historically a billionaire (founded and sold Business Wire to Berkshire Hathaway, 2006); estate/foundation assets
prospects.wealth_sources: Business Wire — founded the press-release distribution company, sold to Berkshire Hathaway in 2006; became one of America's most prolific education philanthropists.
prospects.recent_news: Lokey passed away in 2022; his philanthropic legacy is administered through his estate/foundation. His lifetime UO support alone totaled nearly $140M.
prospects.athletics_connection: No athletics giving — Lokey's giving was academic (sciences, faculty, facilities). Included as a benchmark for transformational UO academic philanthropy and as a reminder to engage his foundation/estate stewards for any continued UO priorities.
prospects.philanthropy_history: ~$140M to UO academics (Lokey Science Complex, $74.6M transformational gift in 2007, Faculty Excellence Fund, Allan Price Science Commons, education quad, music building, HEDCO).
prospects.why_prospect: Represents the single largest non-Knight academic benefactor in UO history; while deceased, his foundation/estate stewards remain relevant relationships for the UO advancement ecosystem (note: athletics is outside his demonstrated intent).
prospects.engagement_angle: Engagement here is with estate/foundation trustees and would be academic-aligned; not a primary athletics target but important context for UO's overall principal-gift landscape.
prospects.urgency_flag: Estate is in legacy-execution phase; relationships should be maintained at the foundation/trustee level.
sources: Help UO Matters compile list of UO's largest donors, https://uomatters.com/2015/05/help-uo-matters-compile-list-of-uos-largest-donors.html

prospects.name: Renée J. James
prospects.uo_connection: BA International Business 1986; MBA 1992, both from University of Oregon. Current UO Board of Trustees member.
prospects.current_role: Founder and former Chairman/CEO of Ampere Computing; Operating Executive at The Carlyle Group; independent director at Citigroup; former President of Intel
prospects.wealth_sources: 28-year career at Intel (rose to President); founder/CEO of Ampere Computing, a semiconductor (Arm server chip) company sold to SoftBank for $6.5B in 2025; private equity (Carlyle); board compensation (Citigroup, formerly Oracle/Vodafone)
prospects.recent_news: On March 19, 2025, SoftBank Group announced acquisition of Ampere Computing for $6.5 billion in an all-cash deal, set to close in the second half of 2025. As Ampere's founder and major equity holder, James experienced a significant liquidity event.
prospects.athletics_connection: No publicly documented athletics gift to date; serves on UO Board of Trustees, giving her direct institutional engagement with university leadership and priorities.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Active institutional leadership via UO Board of Trustees; longtime tech-industry civic/government service (NSTAC chair under Obama). Specific large philanthropic gifts not widely publicized, suggesting untapped major-gift potential.
prospects.why_prospect: James just monetized a multi-billion-dollar company she founded, creating a fresh, large liquidity event ideal for a transformational gift. As a current UO Trustee with two UO degrees, she has deep institutional loyalty and is already engaged with university leadership. Her capacity and recent windfall make her one of the strongest new athletics prospects.
prospects.engagement_angle: Leverage her Board of Trustees relationships and President Scholz's office. Frame an athletics gift around innovation, women's sports leadership, or a technology/performance-science angle (e.g., student-athlete performance analytics) that aligns with her semiconductor/AI background and Ducks pride.
prospects.urgency_flag: HIGH — the $6.5B SoftBank acquisition closed in 2025, creating a near-term liquidity window. Engage promptly while proceeds and tax-planning conversations are active.

prospects.name: Gwendolyn H. 'Gwen' Lillis
prospects.uo_connection: Widow of Charles M. 'Chuck' Lillis (PhD in marketing, UO Lundquist College of Business, 1972; UO's inaugural Board of Trustees chair). Chair of the Lillis Foundation and former UO Foundation board member.
prospects.current_role: Chair, The Lillis Foundation; private investor (family wealth from Lone Tree Partners/Castle Pines Capital and MediaOne)
prospects.wealth_sources: Chuck Lillis built wealth as CEO/chairman of MediaOne (broadband cable spun off from US West) and via private equity (Lone Tree Partners, Castle Pines Capital); board seats at SUPERVALU, Washington Mutual, Williams Companies, Medco
prospects.recent_news: Chuck Lillis died September 10, 2024; the Lillis family legacy and foundation remain active. The passing creates an estate/legacy-giving moment for Gwen and the family foundation.
prospects.athletics_connection: The Lillises' primary UO giving has been academic (lead gift for the Lillis Business Complex; Knight Campus and Ballmer Institute development). No major athletics gift to date — an open opportunity given the family's deep institutional ties.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Made the $14M lead gift for the Lillis Business Complex (opened 2003); central to launching the Knight Campus and Ballmer Institute. Gwen holds a PhD in business and runs the family foundation.
prospects.why_prospect: The Lillis family is among UO's most generous and institutionally engaged donor families, with proven multi-million-dollar giving and significant remaining capacity. Following Chuck's 2024 passing, estate and legacy planning create a natural moment for a memorial or named athletics gift honoring his transformative role as founding Trustee chair.
prospects.engagement_angle: Approach through the UO Foundation and President's office with a tribute concept honoring Chuck Lillis's legacy as inaugural Board chair — potentially a named athletics facility space or leadership/scholarship fund bridging academics and athletics.
prospects.urgency_flag: MEDIUM-HIGH — Chuck Lillis's September 2024 death opens an estate/legacy giving window over the next 12-24 months.

prospects.name: Estate / Family of Robert C. 'Bob' Sanders
prospects.uo_connection: Bob Sanders, UO class of 1951, was a fullback on the Oregon football team; his late wife Jane (Daggett) Sanders, class of 1950, was a UO cheerleader. Met as students at UO.
prospects.current_role: Sanders family / RSG Forest Products successors (Bob Sanders deceased); family lumber-industry wealth
prospects.wealth_sources: RSG Forest Products Inc. — a successful West Coast lumber/forest-products business with operations across California, Oregon, and Washington
prospects.recent_news: The Sanders name remains prominent at UO via Jane Sanders Stadium; family stewardship of the athletics relationship continues as a legacy/estate-giving opportunity.
prospects.athletics_connection: Among UO's most significant athletics donors: Bob Sanders gave more than $16M (a $10M lead gift in 2014 plus $6M in 2016) to build Jane Sanders Stadium, the Ducks softball home, honoring his late wife. Also earlier funded Howe Field improvements.
prospects.philanthropy_history: Demonstrated transformational athletics philanthropy ($16M+ for the softball stadium) plus the historic Howe Field upgrades — a clear track record of large, athletics-directed family giving.
prospects.why_prospect: The Sanders family has already made a transformational athletics gift, proving both capacity and deep emotional commitment to Oregon athletics. The family/estate and next generation represent a strong renewal and legacy-giving prospect for stadium enhancements, endowment, or naming continuity.
prospects.engagement_angle: Steward the existing Jane Sanders Stadium relationship with the next generation; propose endowing softball operations/scholarships or a stadium-enhancement fund to extend the family legacy.
prospects.urgency_flag: MEDIUM — estate/legacy and multi-generational stewardship window; engage heirs to sustain the family's athletics commitment.

prospects.name: Estate / Family of Carolyn S. Chambers (Chambers Family of Eugene)
prospects.uo_connection: Carolyn Chambers earned a degree in accounting from the University of Oregon's business school (1953) — the only woman in her class to earn a business degree; former UO Foundation board of trustees emerita chair and Lundquist College Board of Advisors member.
prospects.current_role: Chambers family successors (Carolyn deceased 2011); Chambers Communications, Stahlbush Island Farms (Bill & Karla Chambers), Silvan Ridge Winery, and the Chambers Family Foundation
prospects.wealth_sources: Cable/broadcast TV fortune — founded Liberty Communications (grew to ~19th-largest US cable operator) sold to TCI in 1983; Chambers Communications (KEZI-TV and sister stations, sold for ~$30M in 2014); cable systems sold to AT&T (2000); plus Chambers Construction, real estate (US Bank tower Eugene), wineries, and Stahlbush Island Farms
prospects.recent_news: Following Carolyn's death, heirs have sold and restructured assets (e.g., the ~$30M sale of KEZI and sister stations), generating family liquidity; the Chambers Family Foundation remains an active Lane County grantmaker.
prospects.athletics_connection: Carolyn's UO giving focused on the business school (Chambers professorship, Lillis Complex support, Technology Entrepreneurship Program). No major athletics gift — an open avenue given the family's deep Eugene/UO ties (note: Stahlbush links the Chambers and Storment networks).
prospects.philanthropy_history: Carolyn was named Eugene's Philanthropist of the Year (1994); established the Chambers Family Foundation (1999) and a named UO professorship; major Lundquist College benefactor. Foundation continues regional giving.
prospects.why_prospect: The Chambers family is one of Eugene's wealthiest and most philanthropic dynasties with proven UO loyalty and major-gift history. Multi-generational liquidity from asset sales and an established foundation create strong capacity; athletics is an untapped, locally resonant opportunity.
prospects.engagement_angle: Engage the next generation (Bill, Scott, Liz Chambers) through the UO Foundation and Eugene business networks; honor Carolyn's pioneering legacy with a named athletics or women-in-leadership opportunity. Note Foundation typically funds smaller regional grants, so pursue family/individual major gifts rather than foundation capital grants.
prospects.urgency_flag: MEDIUM — ongoing estate restructuring and asset sales create liquidity windows; engage heirs while legacy planning is active.

prospects.name: Tim Boyle (and Mary Boyle)
prospects.uo_connection: B.A. in journalism, University of Oregon, 1971; longtime major UO donor; the UO Foundation/advancement is headquartered in buildings tied to family-network donors
prospects.current_role: Chairman/CEO (longtime), Columbia Sportswear Company
prospects.giving_capacity: $10M-$25M for a directed UO Athletics priority
prospects.wealth_sources: Columbia Sportswear — joined 1971 after his father's death, built it with mother Gert Boyle from near-bankruptcy into a multi-billion-dollar global outdoor apparel company (Gore-Tex parkas, Bugaboo jacket).
prospects.recent_news: In 2025 his son Joseph 'Joe' Boyle was named co-president of Columbia Sportswear, signaling generational transition. Columbia navigating ~$200M in potential tariff impacts; projected 2025 net sales of $3.33-$3.37B. Launched 'Engineered for Whatever' brand campaign (Aug 2025).
prospects.athletics_connection: Has made personal contributions to UO Intercollegiate Athletics (cited by UO alongside his J-School and business school gifts). Strong Ducks/'Go Ducks' affinity. Apparel-industry peer/ally of Phil Knight (co-funded a higher-ed PAC with Knight and Kilkenny).
prospects.philanthropy_history: $5M to UO (2007); $10M to UO aquatic/life-sciences facility (2016); $10M to UO-OHSU biomedical data science (2019); $5M for business case competition/architecture; multiple seven-figure gifts. Tim and Mary Boyle Charitable Trust.
prospects.why_prospect: A genuine billionaire UO alumnus with a multi-decade, multi-gift relationship to the university and explicit personal giving to Intercollegiate Athletics. The generational handoff at Columbia frees attention/capital for legacy philanthropy.
prospects.engagement_angle: Approach via the apparel/innovation angle (natural Nike/Columbia/Ducks synergy) and his J-School + business-school loyalties; position an athletics naming or performance/innovation facility as a legacy capstone alongside his life-sciences giving.
prospects.urgency_flag: 2025 succession of his son to co-president of Columbia is a classic 'wealth/attention transition' trigger for legacy gift conversations.

prospects.name: Pat Kilkenny (and Stephanie Kilkenny)
prospects.uo_connection: Attended UO (left before completing degree); former UO Athletic Director (2007-2009); longtime UO Athletics booster; former UO Foundation Board of Trustees member; UO Athletic Department Advisory Board
prospects.current_role: Chairman & Majority Owner, Seaview Insurance Co.; Chairman, K2 Insurance Services; co-owner, Aladdin Bail Bonds; founding partner, Division Street (UO NIL collective)
prospects.location: San Diego, California / Heppner, Oregon roots
prospects.estimated_net_worth: $100M-$300M (not publicly disclosed; estimated from sale of Arrowhead and ongoing insurance ventures)
prospects.wealth_sources: Insurance — grew Arrowhead General Insurance Agency from a $5M agency into a ~$1B-premium underwriting operation, sold to private equity in 2006; subsequently founded K2 Insurance Services and Seaview Insurance.
prospects.recent_news: Continues as a founding principal of Division Street, the Phil Knight-backed UO NIL collective (active 2021-present), placing him at the center of UO's NIL/revenue-sharing strategy. Continues leading K2 and Seaview insurance ventures.
prospects.athletics_connection: Exceptionally deep: former UO AD; reinstated baseball and led PK Park development; drove the Matthew Knight Arena project; donated $3M for locker-room renovation, $5M toward PK Park, $1M for the Matthew Knight Arena floor, $1.5M for arena design; estimated $15-20M total to UO.
prospects.philanthropy_history: $15-20M estimated total to UO ($1M+ to academics); Lucky Duck Foundation (homelessness, with wife Stephanie); funded majority of the Bill Moos AD buyout.
prospects.why_prospect: Few prospects combine his level of athletics affinity, operational knowledge of the program, and wealth. He has repeatedly written seven-figure athletics checks and is embedded in UO's NIL future via Division Street.
prospects.engagement_angle: He is a 'pet project' donor — present a specific, tangible facility or program he can champion and brand (as he did with PK Park and the arena). Engage him as an insider/co-architect, not just a check-writer; tie to NIL/revenue-sharing sustainability.
prospects.urgency_flag: College athletics' shift to revenue-sharing/NIL (a Division Street focus) is an active window where his leadership and capital are most relevant right now.

prospects.name: Dave Petrone (and Nancy Petrone)
prospects.uo_connection: BA Economics '66, MBA '68 ('Double Duck'); former UO Foundation trustee; chaired UO's $3 billion campaign cabinet
prospects.current_role: Retired Chairman of Housing Capital Company (US Bancorp JV); former Vice Chairman of Wells Fargo & Company
prospects.location: Palo Alto, CA and Eugene, OR
prospects.wealth_sources: 19 years as Vice Chairman of Wells Fargo in San Francisco, then co-founded Housing Capital Company (residential development lending JV with US Bancorp). Decades of accumulated banking and real estate finance wealth.
prospects.recent_news: Made a recent gift to scale up Entrepreneurs in Residence at the Lundquist College and seed the Oregon Innovation Challenge; established the Nancy and David Petrone Chair in Economics (2018); current chair of the UO Campaign Cabinet.
prospects.existing_uo_giving: Extensive ACADEMIC giving: Warsaw Sports Marketing Center, faculty chairs, economics, journalism, libraries, Black Cultural Center, Women in Flight. Seeded a Ballmer Institute–Athletics partnership but NO transformational ATHLETICS facility/program gift identified.
prospects.athletics_connection: Endowed the Warsaw Sports Marketing/Business Center (sports business education) and seeded a partnership between the Ballmer Institute and Athletics — adjacent to but not a transformational athletics gift. Deep affinity for UO sports business ('We have a dynasty in sports').

As former campaign chair with stated belief that 'we have a dynasty in sports,' he is uniquely warm. His finance wealth and demonstrated $1M+ gift cadence suggest principal-gift athletics capacity.

prospects.current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of Edlen & Company (formerly Gerding Edlen Development); retired CEO of Gerding Edlen

prospects.why_prospect: Engemann sold his firm for $180M nearly three decades ago and has had ample time to compound that wealth, yet his public UO giving is modest and his philanthropic footprint is low-profile — a classic 'undiscovered' high-capacity alumnus.
